paper_sections.title: Glucose metabolism and serotonin receptors in the frontotemporal lobe degeneration.
Positron Emission Tomography Data Analysis and Statistics
Calculation of [11C]MDL100,907 Positron Emission Tomography Binding Images

description.value: The study examined regional cerebral glucose metabolism in patients with the apathetic and disinhibited behavioral forms of the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration and measured cerebral 5-HT2A receptor distribution in a subset using PET.

design.value: An observational case-control PET study of 18 patients with fv-FTLD, divided into apathetic and disinhibited behavioral syndromes, compared with healthy control subjects. Resting-state 18FDG PET was performed in all patients and 24 controls; [11C]MDL100,907 PET receptor studies were performed in 8 patients and 6 healthy volunteers.

clinical_characteristics.value: Signs or symptoms of their disease appeared 6 to 72 months (mean, 28 months; median, 22 months) before this evaluation. Disease severity ranged from 1 to 3 according to a clinical classification. A clinical follow-up for at least 24 months, always confirming the diagnosis of fv-FTLD, was available for all patients.

task_description.value: The in vivo expression of 5-HT2A receptors was evaluated using [11C]MDL100,907 as a tracer in eight fv-FTLD patients and six healthy volunteers.

instrument.value: GE Advance PET scanner (GE-Advance; General Electric Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: A 10-minute transmission scan was started 40 minutes after intravenous injection of 185 to 296 MBq 18FDG and was followed by a three-dimensional static emission scan lasting 15 minutes. Images were reconstructed using the 3D-Re-Projection algorithm, a Hanning transaxial filter with a cutoff of 4 mm, a ramp axial filter with a cutoff of 8.5 mm, and a field of view of 250 mm. Corrections were made for attenuation, scatter, decay, and geometry.

A 10-minute transmission scan was conducted. Three-dimensional dynamic emission scans started with intravenous injection of 19 to 37 MBq [11C]MDL100,907, administered as 5 ml in 10 seconds, and lasted for 60 minutes. The acquisition consisted of four 1-minute, three 2-minute, four 5-minute, and six 10-minute scans. Images were reconstructed using the 3D-RP algorithm, a Hanning transaxial filter with a cutoff of 5 mm, a Hanning axial filter with a cutoff of 8.5 mm, and a field of view of 320 mm. Corrections were made for attenuation, scatter, decay, and geometry.

description.value: PET images were spatially normalized to an 18FDG PET reference template in Montreal Neurological Institute standard stereotactic space and smoothed with a three-dimensional Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: spatial normalization to a 18FDG PET reference template in the Montreal Neurological Institute standard stereotactic space
gaussian smoothing with a 3D kernel of 8 × 8 × 8 mm full-width at half-maximum

model_settings.value: Global differences in tracer uptake, age, and education were considered confounding covariates and covaried out for all voxels; disease duration was used as a covariate of no interest in the comparisons. Comparisons across groups used t statistics with appropriate linear contrasts. The statistical threshold was p < 0.001 and p < 0.01 for direct comparisons.

estimator.value: t statistics with appropriate linear contrasts

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping 2 (SPM2; Wellcome, Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

model_settings.value: Images of binding potential were calculated by dividing pixel-by-pixel radioactivity concentration images collected between 60 and 90 minutes after injection by the mean radioactivity concentration sampled in the cerebellum, which was used as a reference region because its concentration of 5-HT2A receptors is low or negligible.

level.value: image-level binding estimation followed by group-level comparison

estimator.value: reference-region ratio using cerebellar radioactivity concentration
